slides.heading: Dengue Fever
slides.subtitle: A vector-borne Flavivirus infection — fever, bleeding, and plasma leakage.

slides.heading: Overview
bullets: RNA virus, family Flaviviridae, genus Flavivirus; serotypes DENV-1 to DENV-4 (a 5th announced 2013).
Classic signs: Fever, Headache, Anorexia, Malaise, muscle/joint pain + rashes + bleeding.

slides.heading: Vector — Aedes aegypti
bullets: Day-biting (2 hours after sunrise & 2 hours before sundown).
Breeds in stagnant/clean water; low-flying, limited movement.
Fine white dots at the base of the wings; white bands on the legs.

slides.heading: Clinical Phases
rows: FHAMS + joint pain, (+) tourniquet test, biphasic fever (40°C), retro-orbital pain, rash
All bleeding symptoms — hematemesis, bloody stool, menorrhagia; plasma leakage/shock

terms.definition: Capillary fragility test — applicable only in the febrile state; (+) if ≥20 petechiae per square inch.
Blood test — NS1 antigen + antibodies (IgM = new infection, IgG = past infection).

slides.heading: Management
bullets: Fever: tepid sponge bath (25–35°C), paracetamol q4–6h. AVOID aspirin, NSAIDs (bleeding) and corticosteroids.
Anorexia: small frequent feedings; no dark-colored food; low-fat, low-fiber, non-irritating, non-carbonated.
Nose bleed: upright/seated, trunk slightly forward. Gum bleed: ice chips, cold compress on cheeks.

slides.heading: Key Takeaways
bullets: Aedes aegypti, day-biting, breeds in stagnant water; incubation 5–7 days.
Tourniquet test (+) = ≥20 petechiae/sq inch; PCR confirms.
Give paracetamol; AVOID aspirin, NSAIDs, and corticosteroids.
